From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 3:10 PM PST
Subject: Discovery Recap: Embeddings & Reranking - Nova Retail

Hi Elena / Tyler,

Thanks again for the intro call today - appreciated the context. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps so we're aligned. If I mischaracterized anything, flag it and I'll update.

What we heard (pain points)
- Relevance drift on site search - merchandising rules brittle and not scaling with catalog growth.
- Current rerank approach is slow/costly during peak promotions; team needs consistent latency under load.
- Ingestion and vector refresh currently nightly; want faster updates (within an hour) for new SKUs.

Current stack (from your description)
- Embeddings: proprietary on-prem pipeline exporting 1536-d vectors.
- Vector DB: Pinecone (production), snapshot in S3 + Postgres for metadata.
- Index size: ~150M total product vectors, but initial pilot target ~10M (category subset).
- Query pattern: mostly synchronous user requests (low single-digit-second budget) + batch re-rank jobs for email recommendations overnight.

Targets & success criteria
- Latency: p95 end-to-end rerank <50ms (user-facing flows), tail <100ms during modest bursts.
- Cost: steady-state per-query cost target <$0.005 (open to tradeoffs for better relevance).
- Quality: +10% lift in top-3 CTR on search results or measurable increase in precision@10 during A/B.

Pilot proposal (high level)
- 2-week technical pilot indexing ~10M vectors (representative category).
- Integrate with current Pinecone setup or evaluate Redwood's routing/fallback for rerank.
- Provide evaluation harness + sample query set; run offline rerank comparisons + online A/B for a slice.
- Deliverables: performance report (latency/cost), relevance evaluation, infra recommendation and SOW outline.

Next steps (proposed)
1) I'll share a short pilot scope doc + pricing estimate (attached).
2) Tech kickoff with your engineering lead + our SE (Dev Patel) - propose Mon Nov 22, 10am PT.
3) You confirm pilot dataset (10M vector subset) and provide sample query file and an API key or temp access.
4) Procurement: we'll follow up with SOW + PO guidance once pilot scope is confirmed.

Attachments: nova_pilot_scope_v1.docx, redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx

Thanks - looking forward to partnership.

Subject: RE: Discovery Recap: Embeddings & Reranking - Nova Retail (tech notes)

Quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff - copying Marcus for capacity planning.

Questions / assumptions from the call:
- Vector dim: you mentioned 1536 - confirm exact model and whether we can re-encode to 1024/768 for lower storage/latency tradeoffs.
- Update cadence: you asked for sub-hour updates; we’ll need a nearline ingestion path (not just nightly).
- Query QPS: you mentioned 200 QPS bursts during promotions; confirm sustained vs burst numbers so we can size caching.

Recommendations for pilot (10M vectors):
- Indexing: use quantization (8-bit or 4-bit advanced) to reduce memory - for 10M x 1536, 8-bit reduces footprint by ~4x vs float32.
- Serving: recommend a small Dedicated node pool (2 x A100 equiv) for consistent p95 <50ms with KV cache enabled; can scale to 4 nodes for heavy bursts.
- Vector DB: keep Pinecone in the loop for canonical store; we'll run rerank in Redwood and compare end-to-end.
- Batch patterns: for the overnight batch re-ranks keep larger batch sizes; for user-facing servers keep dynamic batching and short timeouts.

Deliverables for kickoff:
- Ingestion plan template + minimal transform script to align dims/metadata.
- Cost/run estimate for pilot (I’ll pull numbers and add to the estimate Marissa attached).
- List of required credentials and S3 paths (please have Nova share before Mon).

I’ll bring a short slide with expected GPU memory and latency estimates for the 10M pilot.
